claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 show a console matching the Xbox One S form factor (white, circular vent, disc slot).
Photo 0 and 2 show two wireless controllers.
Photos show the exterior, but internal cleanliness and wear cannot be fully assessed remotely.
The warranty seal on the back of the console is not shown.
Thermal performance cannot be determined from still photos.
Requires physical testing or a video of peripherals connected.
Photos show controllers, but labels/serial numbers are not visible to confirm they are OEM.
No receipt is visible in the witness report.
No physical game discs or digital library screens were shown.

risks.risk: Internal storage capacity could be the base 500GB rather than 1TB.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the 'Settings > System > Storage' screen.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty or unable to read discs.
risks.proof: A video showing a disc being inserted and the game icon appearing on the dashboard.
risks.if_unproven: as a digital-only console with a broken drive

risks.risk: The console might be banned from Xbox Network/Live.
risks.proof: A video showing the console successfully logging into an Xbox profile and opening the Store.

risks.risk: Controllers may have stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controllers being used in the 'Xbox Accessories' app test mode.

risks.risk: The console may have been opened or repaired despite claims.
risks.proof: A clear, close-up photo of the tamper-evident warranty seal on the rear.

proof_requests: Photo of the warranty seal on the back of the console.
Screenshot of the 'Storage' settings showing total capacity.
Video of the console connected to a TV showing it booting to the home screen and connecting to the internet.
Photo of the UK receipt mentioned.
Video of a game disc being read by the drive.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as an Xbox One S with two controllers. It can be priced based on the worst-case scenario for storage and functionality until further proof is provided.
